question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0,12],$ compute $P(-1\le X\le 3).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0,12],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{12},\, & 0\le x\le 12, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1\le X\le 3) & =P(0\le X\le 3) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{12}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3-0}{12} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
